reason: H0 exercises archive_read_data but never the archive_read_data_block protocol used by copy_file_data_block. It therefore does not directly fuzz block-returned bytes_read/offset values, sparse offset handling, or the error state attached to in_a when archive_read_data_block returns below ARCHIVE_WARN—the exact state whose reporting is corrected in S1.
evidence: The returned offset drives sparse-gap arithmetic and zero filling through offset, progress, sparse, and bytes_read.
On r < ARCHIVE_WARN, S1 changes archive_errno(a) and archive_error_string(a) to archive_errno(in_a) and archive_error_string(in_a), implicating input-archive error-state semantics.
H0 calls archive_read_data(a, data_buffer.data(), data_buffer.size()) and contains no call to archive_read_data_block or observation of block offsets.
recommended_action: Add a harness path that opens attacker-controlled input and consumes entries with archive_read_data_block, validating progress across returned offsets and continuing through retry, warning, EOF, and fatal/error outcomes while querying archive_errno and archive_error_string on the input archive.
